ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on the driver (arrival confirmation was genuine).
ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged, so the case enters through NS-0's driver-cancelled / rider-no-show branch: the driver's cancellation is assessed under NS-1 / NS-2 [F4][F7]. NS-1 (i) is met — the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:14:10 — and NS-1 (ii) is met, since the GPS placed him 41 m from the pickup at that moment, well inside the 200 m radius [F6][F1]. NS-1 (iii), however, fails: after the arrival confirmation the driver stayed within the radius for only 1 min 40 s and cancelled at 14:15:50, short of the required continuous wait of more than 3 minutes [F6][F5][F3]. The driver's message "3 min up, cancelling the trip" at 14:15 does not rescue the fee — the measured wait, not the driver's assertion, governs, and even his own tap-to-cancel interval is under 3 minutes [F10][F6][NS-1]. His post-trip statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited for the rider is likewise a claim that cannot override the GPS and timeline records [F12][F3][F4]. Because one of the NS-1 conditions is not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee is refunded in full, i.e. $6.61 [F7][NS-2]. The NS-2 flag_account limb is not triggered: the trace shows the arrival confirmation was genuine (driver genuinely within 200 m, 41 m at tap, closest approach 38 m), so no fake confirmation occurred [F6][F1][NS-2]. The driver's 90-day record shows one prior upheld no-show dispute, but RD-6 is about route disputes and this is a no-show case where the fee falls away entirely, so no account action is warranted here [F17][RD-6]. No route-deviation segments exist in this case, so segment_findings is empty [F4][RD-1].
